reason: Prof. Sahib Singh reads ਰਸੈ in ਸਾਧ ਸੁਨਿ ਰਸੈ as ਰਸਨਾ ਤੋਂ (from the tongue); add that sense.
In ਤੈਸਾ ਮਾਨੁ ਤੈਸਾ ਅਭਿਮਾਨੁ it is set against honour, so the line needs the sense of scorn received (our Hindi: अपमान).
In ਕਰਣ ਕਾਰਣ the word is commonly read as the created world, with ਕਾਰਣ its cause.
In ਤਿਸਹਿ ਭਲਾਈ ਨਿਕਟਿ ਨ ਆਵੈ it refers to the self-praising man, not to God; the capitalised Him misleads.
In ਤਾ ਕੀ ਨਿਰਮਲ ਸੋਇ the word means renown; that sense is missing.

suggested.hi: पाता है / (पाछै पावै) पीछे पड़ता है

reason: ਮਾਇਆ ਪਾਛੈ ਪਾਵੈ means he runs after Maya, not obtains it.

suggested.hi: धारण करता है / टिकाये रखता है

reason: In ਸਗਲ ਸਮਗ੍ਰੀ ਅਪਨੈ ਸੂਤਿ ਧਾਰੈ God holds creation on his thread; enshrines does not fit.
The literal sense (rot, waste away) is wanted alongside the figurative one.
Enticing suggests temptation; ਮਨੋਹਰ ਬੈਨ in the Saadh's company are pleasing, charming words.
In ਜੋ ਜਾਨੈ ਮੈ ਜੋਬਨਵੰਤੁ (and a12.p4 ਮੈ ਕਿਛੁ ਕਰਤਾ) the word is the pronoun I; that sense is missing.

suggested.en: virtues, praises / qualities (the three gunas of Maya)

reason: In ਤਿਹੁ ਗੁਣ ਤੇ ਦੂਰਿ the word is the three gunas, not virtues or praises.

suggested.en: listen / I listen, may I hear

reason: The Hindi already gives the first-person सुनूँ; the English lacks it, and the -ਉ form is first person here.
Parallel to ਸੁਨਉ in the same stanza, which continues in the first person (ਭਏ, ਹਮਾਰੀ); add the first-person sense.
